title: Cofinal subsequence comparison of strict Roos complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Work in sheaves of $A$-modules and their unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume countable products exist and are exact. Let $X_\bullet$ be a strict inverse sequence of complexes with chain transitions $t_{i,j}:X_j\to X_i$ for $1\le i\le j$, with $t_{i,i}=1$ and $t_{i,j}t_{j,k}=t_{i,k}$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Put $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_{i\ge1}X_i\to\prod_{i\ge1}X_i)[-1]$, with $(s x)_i=t_{i,i+1}x_{i+1}$ and the specified shifted-cone coordinates of [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Let $\phi:\mathbf N_{\ge1}\to\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ be strictly increasing and unbounded, and let $\phi^*X$ have $n$th term $X_{\phi(n)}$ and the composite transitions. The product maps
$$a_\phi(x)_n=x_{\phi(n)},\qquad b_\phi(y)_n=\sum_{i=\phi(n)}^{\phi(n+1)-1}t_{\phi(n),i}y_i$$
satisfy $b_\phi(1-s)=(1-s_{\phi^*X})a_\phi$. Their induced shifted-cone map $r_{\phi,X}:H(X)\to H(\phi^*X)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, natural in strict chain maps of towers. For two such maps $\phi,\psi$ one has
$$r_{\psi,\phi^*X}r_{\phi,X}=r_{\phi\circ\psi,X},\qquad r_{\mathrm{id},X}=1.$$
If a strict compatible family $q_i:P\to X_i$ defines the augmentation $q:P\to H(X)$ with zero shifted-product coordinate, then $r_{\phi,X}q$ is precisely the augmentation with components $q_{\phi(n)}$ and zero shifted-product coordinate. These assertions concern the specified maps of complexes, before localization, and hence their images in the derived category.

proof.text: Write $m_n=\phi(n)$, $P=\prod_{i\ge1}X_i$, $P'=\prod_{n\ge1}X_{m_n}$, $\delta=1-s$ and $\delta'=1-s_{\phi^*X}$. Products of complexes are degreewise. Every coordinate of $a=a_\phi$ and $b=b_\phi$ is a projection or a finite sum of projections followed by chain transitions; hence these define sheaf-module chain maps by the product universal property. All ensuing coordinate computations mean equalities after product projections, so require no assumption that sheaf epimorphisms are sectionwise surjective. In degree $k$, the prescribed Roos coordinates are $H(X)^k=P^{k-1}\oplus P^k$ and $D(y,z)=(-dy-\delta z,dz)$.

source.place: Tag 0H9K, lemma-pro-isomorphism-iso-Rlim, explicit product maps and finite-block elimination; agent refinement to strict complexes

proof.text:
For every $n$, the tower composition law telescopes the finite sum:
$$ (b\delta x)_n=\sum_{i=m_n}^{m_{n+1}-1}t_{m_n,i}(x_i-t_{i,i+1}x_{i+1})=x_{m_n}-t_{m_n,m_{n+1}}x_{m_{n+1}}=(\delta'a x)_n.$$
Thus $b\delta=\delta'a$. Define $C:H(X)\to H(\phi^*X)$ by $C(y,z)=(by,az)$. Since $a,b$ commute with $d$, we have
$$D'C(y,z)=(-bdy-\delta'az,adz)=(-bdy-b\delta z,adz)=CD(y,z).$$
This is exactly the shifted-cone map $r_{\phi,X}$ of the specified square.

proof.text:
Define a degree-zero chain map $h:P\to P$ by the finite formula
$$(hy)_i=\sum_{j=i}^{m_{\nu(i)}-1}t_{i,j}y_j,$$
with empty sum zero. Commutation with $d$ follows term by term. Telescoping gives
$$(h\delta z)_i=z_i-t_{i,m_{\nu(i)}}z_{\nu(i)}^{\rm sel}=((1-Ea)z)_i,$$
where $z_n^{\rm sel}=z_{m_n}$. For $i\ne m_n$ for every $n$, subtracting $t_{i,i+1}(hy)_{i+1}$ from $(hy)_i$ leaves $y_i$. At $i=m_n$, $(hy)_i=0$ and the same difference is
$$-\sum_{j=m_n+1}^{m_{n+1}-1}t_{m_n,j}y_j=y_{m_n}-(by)_n.$$
Hence $\delta h=1-Jb$, including all indices $i<m_1$ by the nonselected case. These are identities of product maps.

source.place: Tag 0H9K, lemma-pro-isomorphism-iso-Rlim, explicit product maps and finite-block elimination; agent refinement to strict complexes

proof.text:
In degree $k$ define $K^k:H(X)^k\to H(X)^{k-1}$ by $K(y,z)=(0,-hy)$. The signed differential of the specified Roos model gives
$$DK(y,z)=(\delta h y,-dh y),\qquad KD(y,z)=(0,hdy+h\delta z).$$
Since $dh=hd$, steps 3-4 imply
$$DK+KD=(\delta h y,h\delta z)=((1-Jb)y,(1-Ea)z)=(1-SC)(y,z).$$
Thus $SC$ is chain-homotopic to the identity with the displayed degree-minus-one homotopy (equivalently $1-SC=DK+KD$), while $CS=1$ strictly.

source.place: Tag 0H9K, lemma-pro-isomorphism-iso-Rlim, explicit product maps and finite-block elimination; agent refinement to strict complexes

proof.text: The sheaf-module category is abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply part (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-homotopic-maps-equal-cohomology], with the identity additive functor and the homotopy of step 5, to obtain $H^k(S)H^k(C)=1$ for every integer $k$. The strict equation $CS=1$ gives $H^k(C)H^k(S)=1$ by functoriality. Thus each $H^k(C)$ is invertible and $C=r_{\phi,X}$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The assumption of exact countable products is retained, although this explicit homotopy argument only needs the products themselves.

Let $f:X_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$ be a strict chain map of towers. Iterating its transition square gives $f_i t^X_{i,j}=t^Y_{i,j}f_j$. Selection satisfies $a_Y(\prod_i f_i)=(\prod_n f_{m_n})a_X$. For the block map, in coordinate $n$,
$$\sum_{i=m_n}^{m_{n+1}-1}t^Y_{m_n,i}f_i y_i=f_{m_n}\sum_{i=m_n}^{m_{n+1}-1}t^X_{m_n,i}y_i.$$
Hence $b_Y(\prod_i f_i)=(\prod_n f_{m_n})b_X$. Taking the two diagonal components of the prescribed cone map proves strict naturality of $r_{\phi,X}$.

source.place: Tag 0H9K, lemma-pro-isomorphism-iso-Rlim, explicit product maps and finite-block elimination; agent refinement to strict complexes

proof.text:
Put $\ell_n=\psi(n)$ and let $a_\psi',b_\psi'$ be the maps for restriction of $\phi^*X$. Selection gives $a_\psi'a_\phi=a_{\phi\circ\psi}$. For the other component, expand the double finite sum:
$$ (b_\psi'b_\phi y)_n=\sum_{j=\ell_n}^{\ell_{n+1}-1}\sum_{i=m_j}^{m_{j+1}-1}t_{m_{\ell_n},m_j}t_{m_j,i}y_i=\sum_{i=m_{\ell_n}}^{m_{\ell_{n+1}}-1}t_{m_{\ell_n},i}y_i.$$
The tower law combines the two transitions and the consecutive intervals partition the displayed finite interval. This is $b_{\phi\circ\psi}y$. Diagonal cone maps compose componentwise, yielding $r_{\psi,\phi^*X}r_{\phi,X}=r_{\phi\circ\psi,X}$. For $\phi=\mathrm{id}$, selection is identity and every block is $[n,n+1)$, so $b_\phi y=y$ and $r_{\mathrm{id},X}=1$.

source.place: Tag 0H9K, lemma-pro-isomorphism-iso-Rlim, explicit product maps and finite-block elimination; agent refinement to strict complexes

proof.text: For a compatible family $q_i:P_0\to X_i$, its product map $q_{\rm prod}$ satisfies $\delta q_{\rm prod}=0$ by the compatibility equation. The strict augmentation is $(0,q_{\rm prod})$ in the coordinates of [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Applying $r_{\phi,X}=(b_\phi,a_\phi)$ gives $(b_\phi0,a_\phi q_{\rm prod})=(0,(q_{\phi(n)})_n)$, exactly the restricted augmentation. All naturality, composition, identity and augmentation equations have been proved as equalities of chain maps. The localization functor preserves these equalities and compositions, and sends the quasi-isomorphism of step 6 to an isomorphism.
